From e9acda52fd2ee0cdca332f996da7a95c5fd25294 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Nikolay Aleksandrov <razor@blackwall.org>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 14:06:59 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] bonding: fix use-after-free due to enslave fail after slave
 array update

Fix a use-after-free which happens due to enslave failure after the new
slave has been added to the array. Since the new slave can be used for Tx
immediately, we can use it after it has been freed by the enslave error
cleanup path which frees the allocated slave memory. Slave update array is
supposed to be called last when further enslave failures are not expected.
Move it after xdp setup to avoid any problems.

It is very easy to reproduce the problem with a simple xdp_pass prog:
 ip l add bond1 type bond mode balance-xor
 ip l set bond1 up
 ip l set dev bond1 xdp object xdp_pass.o sec xdp_pass
 ip l add dumdum type dummy

Then run in parallel:
 while :; do ip l set dumdum master bond1 1>/dev/null 2>&1; done;
 mausezahn bond1 -a own -b rand -A rand -B 1.1.1.1 -c 0 -t tcp "dp=1-1023, flags=syn"

diff --git a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
index a909ebcf1102..45bd2bb102ff 100644
--- a/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c
@@ -2202,11 +2202,6 @@ int bond_enslave(struct net_device *bond_dev, struct net_device *slave_dev,
 		unblock_netpoll_tx();
 	}
 
-	/* broadcast mode uses the all_slaves to loop through slaves. */
-	if (bond_mode_can_use_xmit_hash(bond) ||
-	    BOND_MODE(bond) == BOND_MODE_BROADCAST)
-		bond_update_slave_arr(bond, NULL);
-
 	if (!slave_dev->netdev_ops->ndo_bpf ||
 	    !slave_dev->netdev_ops->ndo_xdp_xmit) {
 		if (bond->xdp_prog) {
@@ -2240,6 +2235,11 @@ int bond_enslave(struct net_device *bond_dev, struct net_device *slave_dev,
 			bpf_prog_inc(bond->xdp_prog);
 	}
 
+	/* broadcast mode uses the all_slaves to loop through slaves. */
+	if (bond_mode_can_use_xmit_hash(bond) ||
+	    BOND_MODE(bond) == BOND_MODE_BROADCAST)
+		bond_update_slave_arr(bond, NULL);
+
 	bond_xdp_set_features(bond_dev);
 
 	slave_info(bond_dev, slave_dev, "Enslaving as %s interface with %s link\n",
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in the bonding driver's `bond_enslave` function. The fix modifies a single file:

**`drivers/net/bonding/bond_main.c`**:
- **Removed** an early call to `bond_update_slave_arr()` that was placed before the XDP (eXpress Data Path) setup code.
- **Added** the same `bond_update_slave_arr()` call *after* the XDP setup code completes.

## Relationship

The bug occurred because the slave was made visible for transmission (by updating the slave array) *before* the XDP setup step. If the XDP setup failed (e.g., because the slave device lacked XDP support), the error path freed the slave memory. However, the slave was already added to the slave array and could be used by concurrent TX paths, leading to a use-after-free when the freed memory was accessed.

By moving the slave array update to *after* the XDP setup, the slave only becomes available for transmission once all enslave steps that can fail (including XDP setup) have succeeded. This ensures that if any error occurs during XDP setup, the slave is not yet visible to TX, preventing the use-after-free.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
- if (bond_mode_can_use_xmit_hash(bond) ||
-     BOND_MODE(bond) == BOND_MODE_BROADCAST)
-   bond_update_slave_arr(bond, NULL);
Reason:
The `bond_update_slave_arr` call was placed before the XDP setup code. If XDP setup fails (e.g., because the slave does not support XDP), the error path (`err_sysfs_del`) frees the new slave. However, the slave had already been added to the slave array, so a concurrent transmission can access the freed memory, causing a use-after-free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
+ /* broadcast mode uses the all_slaves to loop through slaves. */
+ if (bond_mode_can_use_xmit_hash(bond) ||
+     BOND_MODE(bond) == BOND_MODE_BROADCAST)
+   bond_update_slave_arr(bond, NULL);
Reason:
Moving `bond_update_slave_arr` after the XDP setup ensures that the slave is only added to the array after all possible failure points (including XDP setup) have passed. This prevents the use-after-free because the slave cannot be used for transmission before it is fully initialized and safely added to the array.
